title: Midterm elections: How the Democrats beat President Trump’s Republicans
description:
Democrats in the US have won control of Congress in the midterm elections. They’ve done better than even the polls suggested - winning seats held by Republicans for decades. But what does that actually mean?

BBC reporter and What in the World’s resident American, William Lee Adams, breaks down what the elections were for, what voters were most concerned about, what it means for President Trump and his Republican party as well as some of the notable firsts among the victors. And we’re hearing from young voters in some of the states that have changed parties this year

summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart and reporter William Lee Adams analyze the US midterm election results, where Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in a major 'blue wave.' The episode explores how voter dissatisfaction over the cost of living, high fuel and food prices, housing affordability, and foreign policy contributed to Republican losses, especially among young voters. It also highlights several historic firsts among newly elected candidates and discusses how these results will constrain President Donald Trump's legislative agenda during his final two years in office.
